 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn had issues with the officiating on Sunday as Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills secured a 31-12 win.
 The frustration boiled over late in the first half after Jets quarterback Geno Smith absorbed a high-low hit from Bills defenders Terrel Bernard and TJ Parker after releasing a pass. Smith was evaluated for a concussion; no flag was thrown on the play, and Glenn confronted officials near the sideline.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement CBS cameras appeared to capture Glenn arguing that the same hit would have raised flags if Allen had been the recipient.
 NFL Fans Back Aaron Glenn Stance's on Officials
 The exchange quickly gained attention on social media after Awful Announcing shared the clip, with several fans siding with Glenn's apparent complaint and arguing that some quarterbacks receive more favorable treatment from officials than others.
 This NFL fan quoted a video from Awful Announcing's X account and added a short, pithy three-word comment: "No lies detected."
 Another fan agreed with Glenn's apparent complaint, arguing that certain quarterbacks receive preferential treatment from officials.

 The fan posted on social media, "I mean, he's got a point. It's no secret certain QBs get special treatment."
 One NFL observer took up Glenn's complaint and found nothing wrong with it. The person wrote, "Aaron Glenn is many things. But in this instance, he is not wrong."
 Jeff Parles, who is part of the "Cofield & Company" show on ESPN 1100 in Las Vegas, offered a pretty agreeable comment on Glenn's complaint: "AG is 100% right."

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As for this NFL fan, he wrote this on social media while also agreeing with Glenn. The fan posted, "Here's my problem with that, if that was Josh Allen, every flag on the field would be thrown." The realest [expletive] Aaron Glenn has ever said as Jets head coach."
 One more NFL fan kept it pretty simple with this comment posted: "this is facts lol."
 The reactions largely backed Glenn's frustration, with several fans arguing that the no-call on Smith would have been handled differently if Allen had taken the same hit. Others simply agreed that Glenn had a legitimate reason to be upset with the officiating.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Allen was 11-for-21 passing for 196 yards, 1 touchdown, and 1 interception on Sunday. According to the PFN NFL QB Impact Metric , Allen grades out at 81.8, ranking seventh in the league. Those same metrics show Smith grading out at 77.3, ranked 15th.
 In one-plus seasons as Jets head coach, Glenn now has a 5-22 record. The Jets have not been able to put together success in recent seasons.
 Even with that being the case, Glenn, according to most of these fan reactions, appeared to have a solid case on his side. Whether that changes any types of calls made in Allen's favor going forward in the 2026 NFL season remains to be seen.
 This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .
